cards.back: One of the symbols 0 to 9 used to write numbers.
The value a digit has because of where it is in a number.
A group of three digits in a number, separated by a comma.
A number written with digits.
A number written in words.
A number written as the sum of the values of its digits.
Decide whether a number is greater than, less than, or equal to another number.
Change a number to a nearby number that is easier to use.
A number that is close to the exact amount.
The place to the left of the thousands place. Each ten thousand is 10 thousands.
The place to the left of the ten thousands place.

cards.front: How many times as much is a digit worth when it moves one place to the left?
cards.back: 10 times as much.

cards.front: How many thousands are in one million?
cards.back: 1,000 thousands.

cards.front: What do the symbols > and < mean?
cards.back: > means “is greater than.” < means “is less than.” The open side faces the greater number.

cards.front: When you round, which digit do you look at?
cards.back: The digit just to the right of the place you are rounding to. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: round down.

cards.front: In 4,440, how does the value of the 4 in the thousands place compare with the 4 in the hundreds place?
cards.back: It is 10 times as much: 4,000 is 10 × 400.
The zero holds the hundreds place. Without it the number would be 532.

cards.front: How do you compare two numbers with the same number of digits?
cards.back: Start at the left and find the first place where the digits are different.
30,000 + 400 + 5 is expanded form for 30,405. 3 + 4 + 5 only lists digits, so it is not.
6,500 rounds to 7,000. 7,500 rounds up to 8,000.

cards.front: Is 9,875 greater than 12,004 because it starts with 9?
cards.back: No. 12,004 has more digits, so it is greater.
5,000. The hundreds digit is 7, so round up. Do not just drop the digits.

cards.front: Is the value of the 6 in 3,640 equal to 6?
cards.back: No. The 6 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 600.
